mainTopic: The music of the מקדש: trumpet blasts, lyres and flutes, how the blasts are counted, and why the flute played on days of full הלל
overview: The amud opens by finishing a calendar story. A sage shows that the year's full and short months balance out, and רבי יהודה הנשיא praises him as 'נר ישראל'. Then a new משנה sets limits for the music in the מקדש: 21 to 48 trumpet blasts a day, 2 to 6 lyres, 2 to 12 flutes, and twelve days a year when the flute played before the מזבח. It ends with a three-way dispute over who the musicians were. The גמרא shows that רבי יהודה's numbers (7 to 16) differ only in counting: he treats תקיעה–תרועה–תקיעה as one unit, while רבנן count each sound. Each side brings a פסוק from במדבר 10 and answers the other's proof. רב כהנא's rule of no pause at all between the sounds is shown to follow רבי יהודה, based on his words 'ולא כלום'. Finally the גמרא explains that the flute days are days when the full הלל is said, lists those days, and begins asking why סוכות gets full הלל every day but פסח does not. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the calendar calculation
steps.stepSummary: The sage completes his explanation. The leap month had thirty days, and last year two months were made full. These three extra full months balance out this year's three short months.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the added month of the leap year was thirty days, and last year we made both of those months full. So take away the three short months against the three extra full months, and the moon is back in its proper place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story from the previous discussion. A sage is explaining why the moon showed up exactly where the calendar said it should.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some months have 30 days (מלא) and some have 29 (חסר). The extra days added to full months in the past exactly cancel out the days missing from the short months this year. So the calendar ends up lined up with the moon again.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the year a leap year by adding a month
Take away, remove from the count

phrases.english: And the added month of the leap year was thirty days
and last year we made both of them full,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word without 'and'; the square brackets give the corrected wording, which adds it. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: take away three against three
phrases.notes: The three short months this year cancel out the three extra full months from before.

phrases.english: and it stands in its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a calendar explanation that began before this section
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra full months balance out the short months, so the moon is back in line with the calendar

steps.title: רבי confirms and praises the sage
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה הנשיא praises the sage as 'נר ישראל' and confirms that the calculation is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Lamp of Israel! That is exactly how it was.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה הנשיא agrees with the explanation and praises the sage who gave it. This closes the calendar story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כן הוה' means the calculation matches what really happened that year. The title 'נר ישראל' is high praise for someone who lights up the people with Torah wisdom.

keyTerms.meaning: Lamp of Israel, a title of praise for a great sage
So it was, that is correct

steps.whatToRemember: The calendar story ends with full agreement: the moon's position fit the count of full and short months.

phrases.english: He said to him: Lamp of Israel!
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי יהודה הנשיא, praising the sage who explained the calendar.

phrases.english: So it was.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל! כֵּן הָוֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the explanation given in step 1
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The calculation was correct; the moon matched the calendar.

steps.title: Minimum and maximum trumpet blasts in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that the מקדש never had fewer than 21 trumpet blasts in a day and never more than 48.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We do not blow fewer than twenty-one trumpet blasts in the Temple, and we do not add more than forty-eight.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the smallest and largest number of trumpet blasts blown in the מקדש on a single day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal day had 21 blasts: 3 for opening the gates, 9 for the morning תמיד, and 9 for the afternoon תמיד. The most, 48, came on a Friday of סוכות, which added blasts for drawing water, for the מוספין, and to announce שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not go below, the minimum
And we do not add beyond, the maximum

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַחַת תְּקִיעוֹת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: We do not do fewer than twenty-one blasts in the Temple,
and we do not add beyond forty-eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַחַת תְּקִיעוֹת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the Temple's trumpet blasts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daily blasts in the מקדש range from 21 to 48.

steps.title: How many lyres and flutes were played
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the range for instruments: two to six lyres, and two to twelve flutes.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not use fewer than two lyres, and we do not add more than six. We do not use fewer than two flutes, and we do not add more than twelve.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the same pattern of minimum and maximum, now for the instruments that played with the לוים' song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each instrument has its own range. Lyres (נבלים) go from 2 to 6, and flutes (חלילים) go from 2 to 12.

phrases.english: We do not use fewer than two lyres,
and we do not add beyond six.
We do not use fewer than two flutes,
and we do not add beyond twelve,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same minimum and maximum pattern, now for instruments

steps.title: The twelve days the flute played before the altar
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the twelve days a year when the flute played before the מזבח: both פסח sacrifices, the first day of פסח, שבועות, and all eight days of סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: On twelve days of the year the flute played before the altar: at the slaughtering of the first פסח offering, at the slaughtering of the second פסח offering, on the first יום טוב of פסח, on the יום טוב of שבועות, and on the eight days of סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us which special days had flute music before the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Add them up: פסח ראשון (1), פסח שני (1), the first day of פסח (1), שבועות (1), and the eight days of סוכות (8). That makes twelve.

keyTerms.meaning: The main פסח offering, brought on 14 ניסן
The makeup פסח offering, brought on 14 אייר

steps.confusionAlert: 'עצרת' here means שבועות, not שמיני עצרת. 'החג' on its own means סוכות.

phrases.english: And on twelve days of the year
the flute plays before the altar:
at the slaughter of the first Paschal offering,
and at the slaughter of the second Paschal offering,
and the first festival day of Passover,
and on the festival of Shavuot,
and on the eight days of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר יוֹם בַּשָּׁנָה הֶחָלִיל מַכֶּה לִפְנֵי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail about when the flutes from step 4 were played
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The flute played before the מזבח on twelve set days a year.

steps.title: Why a reed flute, and why a single flute at the end
steps.stepSummary: The flute was made of reed, not copper, because reed sounds sweeter. The music ended with one single flute because that makes a nicer finish.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would not play a copper pipe, only a reed pipe, because its sound is sweet. And he would end the music only with a single pipe, because it finishes nicely.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two details about how the flute was played, each with a reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rules are about making the music beautiful. Reed was chosen over copper for its pleasant sound, and a single flute was used for the final notes so the ending would be smooth.

keyTerms.meaning: Ends the music, plays the closing notes

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה sets limits and choices for the מקדש music: 21 to 48 blasts, 2 to 6 lyres, 2 to 12 flutes, twelve flute days, a reed flute, and a single flute to finish.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה מַכֶּה בְּאַבּוּב שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת,
phrases.english: And he would not play with a copper pipe,
but rather with a reed pipe,
because its sound is pleasant;

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה מְחַלֵּק אֶלָּא בְּאַבּוּב יְחִידִי,
phrases.english: and he would conclude only with a single pipe,
phrases.notes: 'מחלק' here means playing the closing notes of the music.

phrases.english: because it concludes nicely.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא הָיָה מַכֶּה בְּאַבּוּב שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds details about the kind of flute and how the music ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Use a reed flute, not copper, and end the music with one flute.

steps.title: Who were the Temple musicians?
steps.stepSummary: A three-way dispute over who played the music: רבי מאיר says slaves of כהנים, רבי יוסי says respected Israelite families from עמאום, and רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were slaves of כהנים, says רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says: the families of בית פגרים and בית ציפרא from עמאום, whose daughters married into the כהונה. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: they were לוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a dispute among three תנאים about who the musicians were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion gives the musicians a higher status than the one before. רבי מאיר says they were slaves of כהנים. רבי יוסי says they were Israelites with such clean family lines that כהנים married their daughters. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says they were actual לוים.

keyTerms.meaning: They married their daughters to כהנים, which shows a clean family line
Members of the tribe of לוי

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute sets up the coming discussion about how important the instrument music was to the עבודה, and whether non-לוים could play it.

phrases.english: And they were slaves of priests,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the musicians who played in the מקדש.

phrases.english: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir;
Rabbi Yosei says:
the family of the house of Pegarim and the house of Tzippara
from Emaum, who would marry their daughters into the priesthood;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר: לְוִיִּם הָיוּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says: They were Levites.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַבְדֵי כֹּהֲנִים הָיוּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After describing the instruments, the משנה asks who played them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three opinions: slaves of כהנים (רבי מאיר), respected Israelite families (רבי יוסי), and לוים (רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס).

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה's numbers (21 to 48 blasts) do not match רבי יהודה, who says no fewer than 7 and no more than 16.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Our משנה is not like רבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says: one may not blow fewer than seven blasts, and one may not blow more than sixteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by bringing a ברייתא where רבי יהודה gives different numbers than our משנה. This sets up the question of what exactly they are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 21 to 48. רבי יהודה says 7 to 16. Notice that 21 ÷ 3 = 7 and 48 ÷ 3 = 16, which is a hint that this may be a counting difference and not a real difference in how many sounds are blown.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not go below (a minimum)
One may not add beyond (a maximum)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Our Mishnah is not in line with Rabbi Yehuda,
as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One may not blow fewer than seven,
and one may not add beyond sixteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's ruling on 21–48 blasts (step 3) and shows that a different תנא disagrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the daily blasts in the מקדש are no fewer than 7 and no more than 16.

steps.title: The argument is only about how to count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the disagreement is about. רבי יהודה counts תקיעה–תרועה–תקיעה as one unit. רבנן count each of the three sounds separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree? רבי יהודה holds that a תקיעה, תרועה and תקיעה together are one unit. רבנן hold that a תקיעה is its own unit, a תרועה is its own unit, and the last תקיעה is its own unit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the two sides are really arguing about and answers right away. It is a counting question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on what is actually blown. רבי יהודה counts each set of three sounds as 1, so he gets 7 to 16. רבנן count each sound as 1, so the same blowing comes out to 21 to 48.

keyTerms.meaning: It is one (counted as one unit)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה wants fewer sounds in the מקדש. The actual blowing is the same. Only the way of counting is different.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
Rabbi Yehuda holds:
tekia, terua, and tekia are one unit,
and the Rabbis hold: a tekia is on its own,
and a terua is on its own, and a tekia is on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the number gap from step 8 as a difference in how the blasts are counted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle lies behind the different numbers?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה counts תקיעה–תרועה–תקיעה as one unit. רבנן count each sound separately.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's source: the תרועה is called a תקיעה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's reason comes from two פסוקים that use the verb 'to blow a תקיעה' for a תרועה. This shows the three sounds are bound together as one unit.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי יהודה's reason? It is written: 'And you shall blow (ותקעתם) a תרועה,' and it is written: 'A תרועה they shall blow (יתקעו).' Learn from this that תקיעה, תרועה and תקיעה are one unit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה counts the three sounds as one. It answers with a proof from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה uses a word from the root תקע (the word for a תקיעה) to describe blowing a תרועה. רבי יהודה learns that a תרועה never stands alone. It is wrapped together with its תקיעות into one package.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall blow (from the root of תקיעה)

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
It is written: "And you shall sound a terua,"
and it is written: "A terua they shall sound" (for you),
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:6. The word in round brackets isn't in the פסוק itself, and some versions leave it out.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: תְּקִיעָה תְּרוּעָה וּתְקִיעָה — חֲדָא הִיא.
phrases.english: Learn from this: tekia, terua, and tekia are one unit.
phrases.notes: The proof is that the תורה uses the תקיעה verb (תקע) for a תרועה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for רבי יהודה's view from step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that תקיעה–תרועה–תקיעה is one unit
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 10:5–6, where a תרועה is described with the verb of תקיעה

steps.title: רבנן read the same פסוקים differently
steps.stepSummary: רבנן say these פסוקים teach something else: every תרועה needs a plain blast before it and after it. They do not teach how to count the sounds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן? That פסוק comes to teach that there is a plain blast before the תרועה and a plain blast after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבנן deal with רבי יהודה's proof. They give the פסוקים a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן agree the פסוקים link תקיעה to תרועה. For them, though, the link only tells you the order of the blowing (תקיעה, then תרועה, then תקיעה). It does not mean the three count as one unit.

keyTerms.meaning: A plain, straight blast (another name for a תקיעה)
That is what it comes (to teach)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? That comes for a plain blast before it
phrases.notes: "Plain blast" means a תקיעה, the straight sound.

phrases.english: and a plain blast after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns aside the proof brought for רבי יהודה in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from the פסוקים, not the פסוקים themselves
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוקים teach the order of the blasts (a תקיעה before and after each תרועה), not that they count as one unit.

steps.title: רבנן's source: a תקיעה alone when gathering the people
steps.stepSummary: רבנן prove their view from the פסוק that says to blow a תקיעה without a תרועה when gathering the people. If the three sounds were one unit, the תורה would be commanding half a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is רבנן's reason? It is written: 'And when gathering the congregation, you shall blow a תקיעה and not a תרועה.' If you thought תקיעה, תרועה and תקיעה are one unit, would the Merciful One tell us to do half a מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבנן's own proof from a פסוק. It argues that a single תקיעה must count as a complete unit by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה commands a תקיעה alone, with no תרועה. If only the full three-sound set counted, that lone תקיעה would be just a piece of a מצוה. The תורה would not command half a מצוה, so each sound must count on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: If it would enter your mind (if you thought)

phrases.english: And what is the reason of the Rabbis?
As it is written: "And when gathering the congregation
you shall sound a tekia and not sound a terua."
And if you would think
that tekia, terua, and tekia are one unit,
would the Merciful One say: do half a מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defended רבנן against רבי יהודה's proof (step 11), the גמרא now brings רבנן's own proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבנן's view that each sound counts on its own
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 10:7, a lone תקיעה for gathering the people

steps.title: רבי יהודה: that תקיעה was only a signal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that the lone תקיעה for gathering the people was not a מצוה blowing at all. It was just a signal to call people together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? That was merely a signal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יהודה turns aside רבנן's proof. The lone תקיעה was just a signal, so the 'half a מצוה' problem does not come up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן's argument only works if the lone תקיעה is a מצוה. רבי יהודה says it was only a practical call to gather the people. So a real מצוה blowing can still always be a full three-sound unit.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just a signal (not a מצוה act)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides blow the same sounds. רבי יהודה counts each תקיעה–תרועה–תקיעה set as one (7–16), and רבנן count each sound (21–48). Each side brings a פסוק from במדבר 10, and each side reads the other's פסוק in a different way.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda? That is merely a signal.
phrases.notes: He means the תקיעה for gathering the people was a call to assemble, not a מצוה blowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns aside רבנן's proof from step 12, leaving both opinions standing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lone תקיעה when gathering the people was a signal, not a מצוה, so it does not show that a single sound counts as a full unit.

steps.title: Whose view does רב כהנא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion matches רב כהנא's rule that there is no gap at all between a תקיעה and a תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches what רב כהנא said: 'There is nothing at all between a תקיעה and a תרועה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a rule from רב כהנא and asks which side of the argument it fits. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא says the שופר sounds must follow each other with no break. The גמרא wants to connect this to the argument between רבי יהודה and רבנן from the earlier steps about whether the sounds form one unit.

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which Rav Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין תְּקִיעָה לִתְרוּעָה וְלֹא כְּלוּם?
phrases.english: There is nothing between a tekia and a terua at all?
phrases.notes: He means there should be no pause between the sounds. They are blown one right after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the רבי יהודה / רבנן argument to a later rule of an אמורא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view is the basis of רב כהנא's rule

steps.title: It follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב כהנא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? רבי יהודה's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: רב כהנא's rule fits רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that תקיעה–תרועה–תקיעה is one unit. If they are one unit, it makes sense that you cannot put a break between them.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב כהנא follows רבי יהודה, who treats the three sounds as one unit

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: why say this at all, if it is obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that linking רב כהנא to רבי יהודה is so clear that there was no need to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sounds are one unit only according to רבי יהודה, then a rule against any break obviously comes from him. So why did the גמרא bother to point it out?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 15 needed to be said
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to identify רב כהנא with רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The link seems self-evident, so stating it adds nothing

steps.title: We might have thought רב כהנא fits רבנן too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains it is not obvious. We might think רב כהנא agrees with רבנן and only rejects רבי יוחנן, who allows long gaps.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that it fits even רבנן, and that it only comes to reject רבי יוחנן, who says: if someone heard nine blasts at nine different hours of the day, he has fulfilled his obligation. So it teaches us that it follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the link was needed. Without it, we might have read רב כהנא as only ruling out very long breaks, which even רבנן could accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן allows huge gaps, even hours, between the blasts. We could have thought רב כהנא only meant 'no long gaps like that,' which fits רבנן too. The גמרא teaches that he means no gap at all, which fits רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken first thought)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of gap. רבי יוחנן is talking about hours between blasts. רב כהנא forbids even a tiny pause.

phrases.english: Lest you say: it comes even in accordance with the Rabbis,
and to exclude the view of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמַע תֵּשַׁע תְּקִיעוֹת בְּתֵשַׁע שָׁעוֹת בַּיּוֹם — יָצָא.
phrases.english: If one heard nine blasts in nine hours of the day, he has fulfilled his obligation.
It teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a reasonable mistaken reading the statement prevents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב כהנא might only reject רבי יוחנן's long gaps, fitting רבנן too
steps.terutzMaskana: רב כהנא forbids any pause, which fits only רבי יהודה

steps.title: Maybe that is really what he meant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: perhaps רב כהנא really does follow רבנן and only rejects רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is really so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. Maybe the 'mistaken' reading is actually correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 called the רבנן reading a mistake. Now the גמרא asks why we can't accept it: רב כהנא could hold like רבנן and just be ruling out long gaps.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it is indeed so

phrases.english: But say it is indeed so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection of the הוה אמינא in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב כהנא does not fit רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing so far forces us to reject the reading that he follows רבנן

steps.title: The words 'not at all' prove it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from רב כהנא's own wording. 'ולא כלום' means no pause whatsoever, which fits רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the meaning of 'not at all'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the exact words רב כהנא used. 'Not at all' only makes sense if he forbids even a tiny break.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב כהנא only wanted to rule out gaps of hours, he would not need to say 'not at all.' That strong phrase shows he allows no pause of any size, so he follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא's rule of no pause at all between תקיעה and תרועה follows רבי יהודה. We know this from his strong words 'ולא כלום'.

phrases.english: If so, what is the meaning of "at all"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 from the wording of רב כהנא's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב כהנא might hold like רבנן
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ולא כלום' shows no pause at all, like רבי יהודה

steps.title: Why the חליל on these twelve days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about the twelve days the חליל was played and asks what is special about these days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'On twelve days a year the חליל plays, and so on.' What is different about these days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה and asking why these days in particular were chosen. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists twelve days when the flute was played before the מזבח. The גמרא wants the reason these days, and not others, made the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Flute, played in the בית המקדש

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר יוֹם בַּשָּׁנָה מַכֶּה בֶּחָלִיל וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: On twelve days in the year the flute plays, etc.
What is different about these?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר יוֹם בַּשָּׁנָה מַכֶּה בֶּחָלִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason these twelve days were chosen for playing the חליל

steps.title: These are the days of full הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that on these days an individual says the complete הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because on them an individual completes the הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: the חליל was played on the days when the full הלל is said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The days in the משנה's list are days when the complete הלל is said, days of special joy. That is the reason given for playing the flute on them. This links the music in the מקדש to the days of full praise.
steps.whatToRemember: The חליל was played on the days listed in the משנה because these are days on which an individual says the full הלל.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְיָחִיד גּוֹמֵר בָּהֶן אֶת הַהַלֵּל.
phrases.english: Since an individual completes the hallel on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְיָחִיד גּוֹמֵר בָּהֶן אֶת הַהַלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: These are the days on which the full הלל is said

steps.title: The list of days for the complete הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, lists the days on which an individual says the complete הלל: eighteen in ארץ ישראל and twenty-one in the גולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: there are eighteen days on which an individual says the complete הלל. These are the eight days of סוכות, the eight days of חנוכה, the first יום טוב of פסח, and the יום טוב of שבועות. In the גולה there are twenty-one: nine days of סוכות, eight days of חנוכה, two days of יום טוב of פסח, and two days of יום טוב of שבועות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for its answer in step 21, that these are days when the complete הלל is said. It quotes an actual list of those days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 claimed that the days in the משנה are special because the full הלל is said on them. Here the גמרא backs this up with a known teaching that counts exactly which days get the full הלל. The count is higher in the גולה because an extra day of יום טוב is kept there.

keyTerms.meaning: Eighteen days, the count of full-הלל days in ארץ ישראל
The lands outside ארץ ישראל, where an extra day of יום טוב is kept
Festival days, days of יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this list of eighteen days of הלל with the משנה's list of twelve days when the חליל was played. They are two different lists, and the גמרא brings this one only to show what makes those days special.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the basic source for which days get the complete הלל, a practice still followed today.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan says
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
There are eighteen days
on which the individual completes the hallel:
the eight days of the Festival,
phrases.notes: "The Festival" means סוכות. The eighth day, שמיני עצרת, is counted with it.

phrases.english: and the eight days of Hanukkah,
and the first festival day of Pesach,
and the festival day of Atzeret (Shavuot);
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word "first" in round brackets and some leave it out, since שבועות has only one day in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: and in the Diaspora, twenty-one:
the nine days of the Festival,
and the eight days of Hanukkah,
and the two festival days of Pesach,
and the two festival days of Atzeret.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 21's answer that these are days of complete הלל.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 21 that the special days are days when an individual says the complete הלל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק listing 18 days, or 21 in the גולה.

steps.title: Why every day of סוכות but not of פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the complete הלל is said on every day of סוכות, but not on every day of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about סוכות, that we say the complete הלל every day, and what is different about פסח, that we do not say it every day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices something odd in the list and asks about it. It is setting up an explanation for why סוכות and פסח are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the list, all eight days of סוכות get the full הלל, but only the first day of פסח does. Both are week-long holidays, so the גמרא wants to know what makes them different.

phrases.english: What is different about the Festival (Sukkot)
that we say it every day,
and what is different about Pesach
that we do not say it

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא בְּחַג דְּאָמְרִינַן כֹּל יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a difference that shows up inside the list brought in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the complete הלל is said every day of סוכות but not every day of פסח.
